title: Behind the Business: How Origination finds what’s next
summary: Building long-term value for Phillips 66 by connecting customers, supply and market insight.
body_markdown:
Building long-term value for Phillips 66 by connecting customers, supply and market insight


**What’s next?** Origination is looking for the answer — and turning opportunity into action.


A new video series, “ *Behind the Business* ,” takes viewers inside the people, capabilities and connections shaping Phillips 66’s growth.


In the first episode, **Dan O’Donnell** , vice president of global origination, explains:


- What origination is.
- How his team identifies new customers, sources of supply and market opportunities.
- Connects those three with the right Phillips 66 capabilities.


**Why presence matters**


The episode also spotlights Latin America, where a new office in Bogotá, Colombia is expanding the company’s global origination network. “Having the global origination and global commercial and trading teams with a presence in those regions allows us to stay closer to our core business,” O’Donnell explained.


> “By not having a presence in these key locations, you’re at risk of missing something that is just fundamentally critical to your business.”
>
>
> Dan O’Donnell


**Delivering enterprise value**


During[Phillips 66’s third-quarter earnings call,](https://investor.phillips66.com/events-and-presentations/?_gl=1*1kz3fqv*_ga*MTA5Nzc4ODQxOS4xNzYzMDU5MzE5*_ga_TRFNCWDYLY*czE3OTM5MTQ4MzYkbzE3MCRnMCR0MTc5MzkxNDgzNiRqNjAkbDAkaDE4Mzc3Mjc1NDQ.) Brian Mandell, executive vice president of marketing and commercial, said Commercial’s role is “to extract the integration value between the assets and then to extract all the optionality in any individual asset.”


Mandell connected that strategy to Commercial’s expanding global footprint, announcing Bogotá as the next addition to offices in Houston, Calgary, London, Hamburg, Singapore and Beijing.


Mandell noted Commercial’s global reach is translating into measurable value with Commercial contributing to corporate ROCE by about 2% to 2.5%.


Watch the first episode of “Behind the Business” to learn more.
